# Smithland Lock and Dam

## Location
Smithland Lock and Dam is located on the **Ohio River** near Smithland, Kentucky, at approximately river mile 918.5. It sits near the confluence of the Ohio and Cumberland Rivers.

## Basic Information
- **Operator**: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Louisville District)
- **Completed**: 1980
- **Type**: Wicket dam (one of the last on the Ohio River system)

## Specifications
- **Lock dimensions**: 1,200 feet long × 110 feet wide
- **Lift**: Approximately 22 feet (varies with river conditions)
- The dam uses a system of wickets that can be raised or lowered depending on river levels

## Purpose
- Maintains a navigable channel on the Ohio River
- Supports commercial barge traffic (coal, grain, petroleum, and other commodities)
- Part of the inland waterway system connecting the Mississippi River to the eastern United States

## Notable Features
- One of the high-use facilities on the Ohio River
- The wicket design allows the dam to be lowered during high water, permitting vessels to pass directly over it
- Handles significant commercial tonnage annually
